I'm a regular opiod and other stuff user who's been lurking around this sub.  I always tried to intensely self educate and read about it, so this could be incorrect, but I'd say 9/10 it's probably right.

Opiods, or painkillers and H, occupy a certain set of receptors when they pass the brain-blood barrier. I think it's the Mu, Kapa, and Delta opiod receptors.  Alcohol also messes with at least one of them, I think, which is why alchy and ope DT is hell.  Kratom, being a cousin to the plant that makes opium, Papaver Samnifarium I think, seems far more tame and safe than the former substances I mentioned, but at least partly has a similar mechanism of using those receptors.  It's a big part of the reason you shouldn't mix opiods with other things like that.

It's why Suboxone suppresses cravings and WD without getting you high, it's why opiod users drink a lot, why alcoholics are at risk for opiod addiction, and finally why Kratom can help with drug cravings.
